summary: Shadow warmup pressure from customer analytics sidecar causing reserved pool throughput drop and autoscaler underreaction
description:
Issue summary:
NimbleSearch reported a sustained mid-day throughput degradation (p50 stable, p99 up 3x) on their dedicated reserved pool. Impacted routes are primarily short-listing and realtime-analytics embedding routes that hit gpt-neox-20b-q4 and redwood-embed-1.

Impact:
- Customer facing increased tail latency and reduced effective throughput on reserved pool (estimated 18% token throughput loss during window).
- Some requests hit 5xx timeouts when GPU attach could not be obtained quickly enough.
- Business impact: user-facing search latency spikes for ~60 minutes during daily analytics sampling window.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool (tenant: nimblesearch-dedicated-us-east)
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Run steady production traffic for nimblesearch tenant (mostly short inference requests, average tokens per request 12).
2) Enable analytics-sidecar sampling with 30s sampling window (customer config).
3) Observe autoscaler behavior during sampling pulse (look at p99 and attach latencies).

Observed behavior:
- Autoscaler metrics (replica_count) temporarily do not increase fast enough.
- Numerous short-lived connections keep slots warm and prevent efficient batching/prefetch.
- KV cache churn observed causing memory fragmentation and occasional OOM-driven evictions.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler to detect burst and scale preemptively; streaming/short requests should not prevent prefetch/attach efficiency.
logs:
Selected log snippets and telemetry references:
- attach_latency spikes in timeline: 2026-03-12T10:29:30Z -> p99 1.9s, 10:30:00Z -> p99 2.7s.
- scheduler: failed_attach_count increased from baseline ~4/min to ~25/min during pulse.
- serving-runtime GC/evict logs: "prefetch_eviction: tenant=nimblesearch size=212MB -> force-evict" repeated.
- Connection traces: many short-lived keepalive connections with header X-Sidecar-Sampled: true.
- Autoscaler metrics: replica_cpu_util median unchanged but short_stream_count metric (internal) surged ~7x.

Related dashboards:
- https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/throughput/nimblesearch-reserved-pool
- https://datadog.redwood.internal/logs?query=nimblesearch+prefetch_eviction
investigation_notes: 10:35 - Support triaged and confirmed pattern: daily 10:30-11:30 sampling pulse from customer's analytics sidecar correlated with throughput drop.
11:00 - Collected packet-level traces; observed tens of short inference requests per second that have keepalive=true and immediate close semantics (small token payloads, ~8-16 tokens).
11:20 - Hypothesis A: small frequent short streams are holding connection/slot state causing slot fragmentation and preventing larger batched requests from filling slots efficiently.
11:45 - Hypothesis B: KV cache churn from many warm but not re-used prefixes caused fragmentation, leading to increased host-side memory churn and occasional evictions on GPUs.

12:10 - Correlation: autoscaler uses 1m average CPU/token_rate which did not reflect short_stream_count; autoscaler therefore underreacted. Short streams inflate warm-connection count while not increasing batch throughput metric.
12:40 - Reproduced locally by simulating sidecar pattern; confirmed attach latency and throughput degradation when short_stream_count high and min_replicas low.

13:00 - Scoped mitigation options: customer-side rate limiting of sidecar, server-side tenant min_replicas pin, autoscaler metric change to include short_stream_count or short_stream_rps as a scaling signal.
13:30 - Eng created a small patch to emit short_stream_count in the autoscaler metrics and a follow-up PR to consider it in scaling policy (see related_github_prs).
comments: Support (Ava): Logging from customer shows sudden sampling pulse at ~10:30 daily. Can we get scheduler traces for that window? (attached dashboards)
SRE (Diego): Collected scheduler and attach logs; attaching internal timeline and candidate root cause: short-stream slot fragmentation + KV churn.

Customer (NimbleSearch - Maya R.): We pushed a new analytics-sidecar release last week; sampling rate was increased to 1% -> is that likely to cause this? We're seeing user complaints about search slowness during the window.
Support (Ava): Yes — the change in sampling cadence aligns with the onset on 2026-03-08. Recommending immediate rollback of sampling increase or apply tenant-side limit to sampling threads.
Eng (Diego): Temporary mitigation applied: pinned nimblesearch min_replicas to 3 for reserved pool and applied a per-tenant connection cap on sidecar-initiated streams. Monitoring for 2h post-change.
Customer (Maya): After applying rate-limit and rolling back sampling cadence, we see p99 latency back near baseline. We'll coordinate to implement a permanent fix.
Eng (Diego): Created PR to expose short_stream_count to autoscaler and proposal doc linked. Will schedule rollout after validation.
resolution:
Workaround and remediation:
1) Immediate: Customer rolled back analytics-sidecar sampling to previous cadence and applied a client-side rate limit (100 rps). Support pinned tenant min_replicas=3 for 24h to remove scaling hysteresis.
2) Short-term platform fix: Added a per-tenant short_stream_connection_cap in serving-runtime to prevent warm-slot hoarding by high-frequency small streams. Deployed as canary to us-east.
3) Medium-term fix: Autoscaler change (PR #4219) to add short_stream_count as a scaling signal and adjust threshold heuristics for short-stream heavy tenants.
4) Follow-up: Runbook entry created for diagnosing short-stream noisy-neighbor patterns and recommended customer-side best practices (sidecar sampling/aggregation).

Status: Mitigations applied and monitoring green for two subsequent daily windows. Engineering rollout of autoscaler metric change scheduled for 2026-03-20 behind feature flag.
